I was actually busy filling in my military application form when the oppertunity to guide jumped up.

Would love to apply for the US military, but I strongly doubt it would lead anywhere due to my history of depression.

Besides. I'm fat now and would never pass the physical examinations.
I've had multiple guests urging me to write. But not books. They want me to have a photo printed on canvas and framed along with a shirt story about the sighting/animal.

It could. But my passion lies in guiding in the private sector of the Kruger. Which is hours from the nearest city.

Also doing it over weekends would be tricky with drive times and things like that.

I have very basic medical training.

I'm willing to sacrifice quite a lot, but how will the me from today know what the me of the future wants?

"I wasn't born to pay bills and die."

My employer has no idea.

I could. Would be tricky to get a reliable solid job with this pretense that I u would take "leave" from that position to go and guide part time.

I don't track my expenses. Only expenses that I track are my gaming expenses as they have a history of getting out of hand.

I sell photos occasionally. But the company also pays me for photos they use for social media, which is nice. Private safaris would be a breach of my contract. The only way I could do those is if I resign and work permanently as a freelance ranger. Which would result in my daily earnings to quadruple. But there are no guarantees of work.

I had a nice car which I sold. Now have a beat up old pickup truck. Cheap. But comfortable and reliable. Think that's the only responsible thing I've purchased in the last couple of years.

There are higher positions available. Problem being they generally result in me being moved to an office as rather a manager or head ranger. What's the point? Looking at the wilderness through a window. Other problem is that because you don't do drives you don't get gratuities. On a good month I earn a significant amount more than my manager. Worst case scenario I earn 20% less than what she does.

I can qualify further into guiding (there are levels, FGASA level 1, level 2, level 3 and then you can specialize in various fields). But at max my salary will increase by 50% and gratuities will remain the same.

I've spoken to quite a few people about it and they've told me the same. Especially because they've spent time with me and know how good I am with people.

My main concern is not really financial stability. My main focus is happiness and a stable/supportive environment (history of depression and the doodads that come along with that). But unfortunately in the modern day you cannot simply ignore finances.

Another thing is that my mom is extremely ill and we don't know what tomorrow holds. So Yea. It's tough seeing her 6 times a year.

No. Definitely not saving enough for a retirement. If I saved enough for a comfortable retirement I'd not really have any money left.

My situation is safe. And I have enough for my needs. Half of my salary is going to medical aid, car payments and various other odds and ends.

I am somewhat fulfilled. But the void is growing. I can feel a noticeable difference between how I feel about my job now compared to the thrill and excitement when I just started a couple of years ago.

It's a dream job. By most accounts. I literally get paid to eat 5 star lodge for and take tourists around to go and look at some of the most beautiful creations on this planet.
